clue.text: Drunk on Adam's ale?

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular name for plain water, and tight is slang for drunk, so the phrase jokingly describes someone tipsy on water; the actual sense is 'impossible to leak through'

explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically: WATER (Adam's ale) followed by TIGHT (drunk). The real meaning, sealed against leaks, is nothing to do with drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful reading splits the word into water plus a slang term for intoxicated, while the dictionary sense is sealed so nothing can seep through.

clue.text: In a frenzy? That's a Frenchman all right!

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French title for a man
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone spots a wild-eyed man and concludes he must be French.
explanation.definitionFit: To run wild in a frenzied, uncontrolled way is the idiom behind the word.

clue.text: Land a quarter, say

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four compass points, a quarter of the compass
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone sells a plot covering a quarter of a district, roughly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A large property of land owned by one person is the core sense here.

clue.text: Gives instruction, note, and suffers for it

parts.note: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale
aches means suffers pain

explanation.surface: A teacher lectures, gets a warning note, and pays the price for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor who instructs pupils is doing exactly this verb, synonym for instructs.

clue.text: Get a switch fitted at the entrance

indicators.note: switch tells us to swap the letters of the words get a around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have an electric switch installed by the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged barrier closing an opening in a wall or fence is a way in.

clue.text: Dog a military man — but not all the time

definitions.text: a military man — but not all the time

explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve, whose part-time members are nicknamed after the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A small burrowing hound breed shares its name with British slang for a part-time soldier of the Territorial Army.

clue.text: The team's far from good. Some 11 prefer that

parts.note: a team is a side, and the possessive gives an extra S
addled, as in a bad egg, is rotten: addle means spoiled, far from good

explanation.surface: A fan grumbles that their team is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 is a cross-reference to 11 across, RIDERS, not a team of eleven players; some horse riders prefer a saddle with both legs on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle letting a horsewoman sit with both legs on one flank was preferred by some equestrians.

clue.text: See tallest building marked in squares

indicators.note: building means constructing something new out of the letters of see tallest

explanation.surface: Look at a skyscraper with a chequered facade.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic pattern of square tiles fitting together without gaps is the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Left surrounded by convenience food in a heap

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the letter for left inside the food word

parts.note: a pie is a ready-made food you can buy and eat easily

explanation.surface: Leftover takeaways piled up in a messy mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack of things laid on top of one another is a synonym.

clue.text: Look over agricultural machinery for a person prepared to do business

definitions.text: a person prepared to do business

parts.note: to con is to study or look over carefully
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A dealer inspects farm equipment before making a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who agrees to supply goods or labour under an agreement for payment.

clue.text: They are up — certain comments will be made!

explanation.walkthrough: A jockey is 'up' on a horse; a rider is also a clause or comment added to a statement or jury verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsemen are said to be up when mounted, and additions appended to a verdict or legal document are known by the same word.

clue.text: Fascinating girl learning garland construction

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: An alluring young woman studies how to make flower garlands.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend a siren on the Rhine lured boatmen to their doom, so her name stands for an enchanting woman.

clue.text: Edward I's extensive support

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so this reads 'Edward I is'

parts.note: long means extensive
shanks are legs, which support the body

explanation.surface: Praise for how broad the backing of a medieval English king was.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall English king Edward I was nicknamed for his long legs.

clue.text: Keeping back outside right for further coaching

indicators.note: outside puts the word for keeping back around the letter for right

parts.note: retaining means keeping back

explanation.surface: A coach holds a player back from the right wing for more practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional instruction to learn new skills is a fresh round of training.

clue.text: Country laity in some confusion

indicators.note: in some confusion means the letters of laity are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lay churchgoers in a Catholic nation are bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation on a boot-shaped peninsula, with Rome as its capital.

clue.text: Is least disposed to leave the shore

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of is least are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone is not at all inclined to go away from the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship departs harbour by hoisting its canvas, so the phrase means embark on a voyage.

clue.text: Running water sounds reasonable

indicators.note: sounds says the word for reasonable is spoken, giving a river name

parts.note: sane means reasonable

explanation.surface: A flowing stream is described as sounding sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river flowing through Paris is a body of water in motion.

clue.text: Neat control

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' here is the archaic noun for oxen or cattle, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, of which a young castrated bull is one; the verb means to guide.

clue.text: Record a bit of music

explanation.definitionFit: To jot something down is one sense; a single musical tone is the other.

clue.text: She's English and retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word and is read back to front

explanation.surface: A shy English woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, standing for any female person.

clue.text: Smoother means of transport

explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's tool shaves wood level, and an aircraft carries passengers.

clue.text: Attending to get something for nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Being there in person is one sense; a gift given free is the other.

clue.text: Some footballers are always over-weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ever means always
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A football team are forever too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is a Liverpool football club. The hyphen in 'over-weight' hides the positional indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merseyside club's squad, so its players are a set of footballers.

clue.text: Knowing about state servitude

indicators.note: about means the word for knowing goes around the other piece

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A shrewd comment on a nation that keeps people in bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of being owned and forced to work for another is bondage.

clue.text: A look of malevolence

parts.note: a glare thought to bring bad luck or harm on whoever receives it

explanation.definitionFit: A wicked stare believed to cast a curse is a hostile glance.

clue.text: Anyway aren't chasing money, having seen the light

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the jumbled letters come after the money

parts.note: L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

indicators.note: anyway means in any order, so the letters of aren't are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone has finally understood that money isn't what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyway' jumbles AREN'T into EARNT, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been enlightened, someone has acquired understanding, a past-tense form of studying.

clue.text: Troubles any son may cause

indicators.note: may cause suggests the letters of any son are rearranged to produce another word

explanation.surface: Any son can cause trouble for his parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritates or bothers, a verb synonym for troubles.

clue.text: Eat daintily but quite a large amount

explanation.definitionFit: A bird pecks at food in small bites; a peck is also an old dry measure, as in 'a peck of trouble'.

clue.text: Unnoticeable part of the listening equipment

indicators.note: part says the answer is a piece of the longer word Unnoticeable

explanation.surface: A tiny component of a hearing aid goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning relating to the ear, which is the body's hearing organ.

clue.text: Adults generally choose to speak out

parts.note: to elect is to choose
to orate is to speak out in public

explanation.surface: Grown-ups as a rule prefer to voice their opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of grown-up citizens entitled to vote, taken as a whole.

clue.text: Sort of wishing well

explanation.definitionFit: A type or category is one sense; benevolent and well-meaning is the other.

clue.text: Pay attention or get the sack!

explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is one sense; to be handed notice of dismissal is the other.
